chunks.arabic_text: رِجَالُ الْكَشِّيِّ: حَمْدَوَيْهَ وَإِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ، عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ

translations.en: Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh and Ibrahim, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Hasan b. Ali

chunks.arabic_text: أَنَّ أَبَاهُ عَلِيَّ بْنَ يَقْطِينَ رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ وَجَّهَ إِلَى جَوَارِيهِ حَتَّى حَمَلَ حَبَاءَهُنَّ مِمَّنْ بَاعَهُ، فَوَجَّهَ إِلَيْهِ بِمَا فَرَضَ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ مَهْرِهِنَّ وَزَادَ ثَلَاثَةَ آلَافٍ دِينَارًا لِلْوَلِيمَةِ، فَبَلَغَ ذَلِكَ ثَلَاثَةَ عَشَرَ أَلْفًا دِينَارًا فِي دَفْعَةٍ وَاحِدَةٍ

translations.en: that his father Ali b. Yaqtin – may Allah have mercy on him – sent to his female slaves [to hand over to him whatever they possessed of wealth] such that he even carried away their gifts [given to them] by the one who sold them to him [their former master], then he sent to him [al-Kadhim] what he [the Imam] had enjoined on him of [collecting] their [al-Kadhim’s sons’ prospective wives’] dowries, and he added three thousand gold coins for the Walima [public lunch], so it all came to thirteen thousand gold coins in a single installment.

en.summary: This narrative from Rijal al-Kashshi highlights Ali ibn Yaqtin's piety and financial generosity as a prominent companion of the Imams, illustrating the practice of sending surplus wealth to the Imam as a form of spiritual investment. The specific mention of the 'Walima' (wedding feast) alongside the dowries underscores the social and religious importance of public celebration in Shia tradition. The substantial sum of thirteen thousand dinars reflects the economic status of the Banu Yaqtin family and their close ties to the Imamate.
en.seo_question: What financial contributions did Ali ibn Yaqtin make to the Imam regarding his slaves' dowries?
